meta.note: Human-produced Cherokee-English sentence pairs, used ONLY as reference translations to test GPT-5.6's raw Cherokee<->English ability before trusting it to translate our own logic items (Part 5.1). Not used as training data.

items.english: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land, unto Gennesaret.

items.cherokee: ᎠᏎᏃ ᏔᎵᎭ ᎠᎴ ᏦᎢᎭ ᎭᎾᏉ ᎠᎾᏁᎳᏗᏍᎨ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎦᎸᎳᏗᏣ.
items.english: But always two or three stayed and set up housekeeping in the doorway.
At this the crowd would yell and cheer.

items.cherokee: ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗᏳᎳ ᏥᏙᎬ ᏥᏯᎦᏎᏍᏗ ᏓᎭᎾᏩᎩᏍᎬ ᏅᏙ ᎠᎦᎵᏍᎬ.
items.english: I stood in the doorway and watched as she undressed in the moonlight.

items.cherokee: ᎤᏰᎸᏗ “ᎤᏨᏉᏗ ᏱᎨᏒᎾ’ ᏃᎴ “ᎦᏙᎯ ᎾᎥᏂ, ᏍᎩᏗ ᏄᏍᏗ ᏫᎵᎻ.”
items.english: It means ‘not proud’ and it means ‘near the ground.’ That’s Wilbur all over.

items.cherokee: ᏌᏊᏃ ᎢᏳᏩᎪᏗ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏚᏃ ᎤᏒ ᎢᎠᎾᎢᏎ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᎢᏗᏜ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᎢᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᏙᎸᎯ.
items.english: One night my grandmother and grandfather were walking home from church.
And a man cannot crawl under a rock and disappear.

items.cherokee: ᏣᏁᎳ ᏐᏁᎳ ᏩᏍᏗ, ᏙᏱᏨ ᎠᎦᎵᏍᎬ ᎤᏢᏅᏍᏗ ᎤᏪᎵᏎ.
items.english: From eight to nine, Wilbur planned to take a nap outdoors in the sun.
Doctors are supposed to understand everything.

items.cherokee: ᎾᎾᏃ ᏩᎭᏯ ᎦᏂᏓᏛ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎦᎴᎾ ᏗᏍᏛᎦᏴᎮᏗ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏁ.
items.english: Then Wolf's tail and ears stiffened.

items.cherokee: ᏐᏉ ᎢᏳᏩᎦᏘ, ᏥᏫᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ, ᎣᎩᎾᎵᎪᏓ ᎡᎲ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ.
items.english: Once when I was a young man, I had a girlfriend.
